question: Can knowability be a property belonging to an entity itself?
premises: If knowability belonged to all knowers, it could not belong to a single knower as such.
Knowability cannot be consistently assigned either to one knower or to all knowers as an entity's property.
A property that cannot be coherently located is not a property of the entity.
inference: Knowability is not any property inherent in an entity.
plain_english: If something were knowable by all knowers, it would not be knowable by a single knower in that exclusive sense. Therefore, knowability is not any property that belongs to an entity.
